comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C2, C3, C22, C30 regarding quadruple mutant viability and characterization as SUPPORTED. Reviewers explicitly praised the mutant generation as a major strength, and OpenEval found converging evidence from experimental observations and functional validation.

Strong agreement on module independence (C23-C29, C96-C97). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes modest cross-talk doesn't invalidate module independence; peer reviewers praised mutations targeting specific immune functions without effects on others. Peer review R2 also includes C31-C32 (cross-regulation), which OpenEval addresses separately in R18.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C4, C68 regarding additive rather than synergistic module interactions as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites systematic assessment across 24 pathogens; peer reviewers found the conclusion about module independence 'compelling' and praised the holistic approach.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C33-C37 regarding collective importance of modules for lifespan as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites survival data showing compound mutant mortality; peer reviewers noted appreciation for the holistic approach without raising concerns about lifespan findings.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C38-C40, C102-C104 regarding melanization and Toll contributions to wound healing as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites clean injury survival data; peer reviewers accepted findings without critique and praised the work on module interactions.

Substantial agreement on pathogen susceptibility patterns (C41-C43 overlap). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on Imd/AMP roles against Gram-negative bacteria and viruses; peer review R5 covers broader pathogen testing including these findings. Reviewers praised comprehensive pathogen evaluation.

Partial overlap on effector analysis (C53, C55-C56, C60). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval R6 addresses AMPs as Imd effectors; peer review R7 covers broader effector dissection. Both align with reviewers' praise for systematic analysis of immune components.

Partial overlap on Toll pathway susceptibilities (C44-C46). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on Toll/Bomanin roles; peer review R5 covers comprehensive pathogen testing including these patterns. Reviewers praised systematic evaluation across multiple pathogens.

Partial overlap on effector analysis (C57-C59, C61). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval R7 addresses Bomanins as Toll effectors; peer review R7 covers broader effector dissection. Both support the manuscript's systematic approach to dissecting downstream effectors.

Strong agreement on melanization's antiviral role (C49-C52). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this as a novel finding; peer reviewers did not challenge this unexpected result and praised the comprehensive pathogen testing that revealed it.

Partial overlap on phagocytosis contributions (C47-C48). Both find evidence SUPPORTED, though OpenEval notes caveats about indirect effects through reduced Imd activation. Peer reviewers praised comprehensive pathogen testing without raising concerns about phagocytosis findings.

Minimal overlap on antiviral roles of AMPs/Bomanins (C62). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights extension of known AMP/Bomanin functions to viral defense; peer review R7 covers broader effector analysis including this finding.

Strong agreement on double mutant analysis (C63-C67). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites comprehensive survival comparisons showing additive/synergistic effects; peer reviewers specifically praised combinatory mutants for enabling study of component interplay.

Partial overlap on microbial load kinetics (C69-C72). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses module-specific contributions to pathogen control; peer review R10 covers broader temporal analysis. Both align with reviewers' praise for revealing timing and interconnections of immune modules.

Strong agreement on S. aureus kinetics (C73-C77). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights temporally distinct module contributions; peer review R10 covers this as part of broader mechanistic dissection. Reviewers praised the temporal analysis approach.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C78-C84 regarding C. albicans defense kinetics as SUPPORTED. OpenEval distinguishes resistance versus tolerance mechanisms; peer reviewers accepted temporal analysis without challenge and praised revelation of module timing and interconnections.

Divergent evaluations. OpenEval rates claims C85-C87 regarding sexual dimorphism as UNCERTAIN due to limited data and unexplored mechanisms. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, explicitly stating appreciation for added female fly experiments showing module function applies to both sexes. This represents a substantive disagreement on data sufficiency.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C89-C95 regarding PLUD analysis distinguishing resistance from tolerance as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this as an important conceptual advance; peer reviewers specifically appreciated investigation of both tolerance and resistance mechanisms.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C20-C21 regarding technical limitations (lethality of certain combinations) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these as experimental constraints; peer reviewers did not question these limitations and praised the overall mutant generation achievement.

Agreement on cross-regulation (C31-C32). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses this separately from main module characterization; peer review R2 includes it with broader module independence findings. Both note cross-regulation doesn't invalidate module independence.
